Title: Verify that a shop owner can create an order for their own shop using JWT authentication
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner has a shop with ID 1. 3. At least one item exists in the shop.

Title: Verify that a shop owner cannot create an order for a shop they do not own
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner does not own shop with ID 2.

Title: Verify that a shop owner can retrieve workers only from their own shop using JWT authentication
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner owns shop with ID 1. 3. Shop with ID 1 has at least one worker.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers?page=0&limit=10 using the JWT token of the shop owner. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify that an expired JWT token returns an appropriate error response
Preconditions: 1. A user has an expired JWT token. 2. The user attempts to access a protected endpoint.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers with the expired JWT token in the Authorization header. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify that an invalid JWT token returns an appropriate error response
Preconditions: 1. A user has an invalid JWT token. 2. The user attempts to access a protected endpoint.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers with an invalid JWT token in the Authorization header. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify successful authentication with valid JWT token for protected API endpoints
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a registered user (shop owner)
Expected Result:
1. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and a paginated list of workers in the 'data' field.
2. HTTP 201 Created response with status 'success', message 'Order created successfully', and the created order details including 'orderId' in the 'data' field.

Title: Verify authentication failure with expired JWT token
Preconditions: An expired JWT token is available for a registered user
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the Authorization header containing 'Bearer <expired-jwt-token>'. Use any shopId.
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized response with a JSON body containing: {"status": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "code": "TOKEN_EXPIRED", "message": "Your session has expired. Please login again."}

Title: Verify authentication failure with invalid JWT token
Preconditions: An invalid JWT token is available (e.g., malformed or tampered token)
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the Authorization header containing 'Bearer <invalid-jwt-token>'. Use any shopId.
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized response with a JSON body containing: {"status": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "code": "TOKEN_INVALID", "message": "Invalid token. Please login again."}

Title: Verify shop owner can access and modify orders for their own shop only
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a shop owner who owns shop with ID 1 but not shop with ID 2

Title: Verify shop owner can add a new worker and set their PIN after OTP verification
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a shop owner who owns shop with ID 1. A worker email is available for OTP delivery.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/1/workers/send-otp with the payload in testData.
2. Retrieve the OTP sent to the worker's email.
3. Send a POST request to /api/shops/1/workers/set-pin with the payload in testData, including the OTP from step 2.

Test Data: Step 1: {
  "name": "New Worker",
  "phone": "+15551234567",
  "email": "worker@example.com",
  "address": "123 Worker St"
}

Step 3: {
  "phoneNumber": "+15551234567",
  "otp": "123456",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "1234"
}
Expected Result:
1. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and message 'OTP sent to your email'.
2. OTP is received at the worker's email address.
3. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and message 'Worker PIN set successfully'. The worker can now authenticate using their phone number and PIN.

Title: Verify the new feature flag 'app.security.config2.enabled' is respected and does not break existing functionality when disabled
Preconditions: 1. Application is deployed with the updated application.properties. 2. No other changes to security-related configurations.
Steps:
1. Start the application. 2. Perform a security-sensitive operation (e.g., login, token generation). 3. Observe application logs and behavior.

Test Data: app.security.config2.enabled=false (new setting)
Expected Result: 1. Application starts without errors. 2. Security-sensitive operations complete successfully without errors or unexpected behavior. 3. No errors or warnings related to 'app.security.config2.enabled' appear in logs.

Title: Verify the application behaves correctly when the new feature flag 'app.security.config2.enabled' is absent or commented out
Preconditions: 1. Application is deployed with the new feature flag removed or commented out from application.properties. 2. No other changes to security-related configurations.
Steps:
1. Start the application. 2. Perform a security-sensitive operation (e.g., login, token generation). 3. Observe application logs and behavior.

Test Data: app.security.config2.enabled (absent or commented out)
Expected Result: 1. Application starts without errors. 2. Security-sensitive operations complete successfully without errors or unexpected behavior. 3. No errors or warnings related to missing 'app.security.config2.enabled' appear in logs.

Title: Verify the project builds successfully with the updated pom.xml and produces the correct artifact
Preconditions: 1. Clean the project (e.g., mvn clean). 2. Ensure no local or remote dependency conflicts exist.
Steps:
1. Run the build command (e.g., mvn clean install). 2. Observe the build output and logs. 3. Check the target directory for the generated artifact.

Test Data: pom.xml (no version changes, only formatting)
Expected Result: 1. Build completes with SUCCESS status. 2. Artifact is generated in the target directory with the correct name (TailorBookApp-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar). 3. No dependency resolution errors or warnings appear in logs.

Title: Shop owner attempts to create an order for a shop they do not own
Section: Order Management - Order Creation / Update Authorization
Preconditions: A shop owner user account exists and is authenticated (has a valid JWT). The owner is associated with shopId 10. A different shop exists with shopId 20.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the shop owner of shopId 10 and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a POST request to /api/orders with a JSON body whose 'shopId' is 20 (a shop the caller does not own). 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"shopId": 20, "customerName": "John Doe", "customerPhone": "01711111111", "customerGender": "male", "paidAmount": 0, "trialDate": "2026-01-20", "deliveryDate": "2026-01-25", "items": [{"itemId": 1, "makingCharge": 50, "measurementGroups": []}]}
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden (or HTTP 401 Unauthorized) with a JSON error body indicating access is denied. No new order is created for shopId 20.

Title: Shop owner attempts to update an order that belongs to another shop
Preconditions: An order with id 555 exists and belongs to shopId 20. A shop owner user is authenticated, but that owner is associated with shopId 10, not 20.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the shop owner of shopId 10 and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a PUT request to /api/orders/555 with a valid update JSON body (any shopId matching order 555's real shop). 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"shopId": 20, "customerName": "Jane Doe", "customerPhone": "01722222222", "paidAmount": 100, "items": []}
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden (or HTTP 401 Unauthorized) with a JSON error body indicating access is denied. Order 555 is not modified.

Title: Authenticated non-admin user attempts to fetch orders for a shop they do not own
Section: Order Management - Shop Order Listing Authorization
Preconditions: A user account exists with role CUSTOMER (or any non-admin role that does not own a shop). That user is signed in and holds a valid JWT. Shop 20 exists and is owned by a different user.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the non-owner user and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/20 with default pagination (page=0, limit=10). 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (no JSON body; URL = /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden with a JSON error body indicating the user does not have permission to view orders for this shop. No order data is returned.

Title: Unauthenticated caller attempts to fetch orders for any shop
Section: Order Management - Shop Order Listing Authentication
Preconditions: No authentication token is supplied on the request. Shop 20 exists.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/20 without an Authorization header. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (no JSON body; URL = /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON error body whose 'code' is 'UNAUTHORIZED' (or similar) and message indicating authentication is required. No orders are returned.

Title: Non-admin caller requests the worker list for a shop they do not own
Preconditions: A user with role CUSTOMER is signed in and has a valid JWT. Shop 20 exists and is owned by a different user.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the non-owner user and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a GET request to /api/shops/20/workers with default pagination. 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (no JSON body; URL = /api/shops/20/workers?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden with a JSON error body indicating access is denied. No worker data is returned.

Title: Authenticated request is made with a tampered/garbled JWT
Preconditions: An authenticated route is targeted. The supplied Authorization header carries 'Bearer ' followed by a syntactically invalid token (e.g. 'abc.def.ghi' or 'not-a-real-jwt').
Steps:
1. Send any request to a protected endpoint such as GET /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10 with the header 'Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-jwt'. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (Header value: 'Bearer not-a-real-jwt'; URL = /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON body whose 'code' is 'TOKEN_INVALID' and a message indicating the token is invalid. No data is returned.

Title: Authenticated request is made with an expired JWT
Preconditions: A previously issued JWT exists whose 'exp' claim is in the past. The Authorization header is supplied in 'Bearer <token>' format.
Steps:
1. Obtain a JWT that has already expired (or wait until a short-lived test token expires). 2. Send a GET request to a protected endpoint such as /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10 with 'Authorization: Bearer <expired-token>'. 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (Header value: 'Bearer <expired-jwt-here>'; URL = /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON body whose 'code' is 'TOKEN_EXPIRED' and a message indicating the session has expired. No data is returned.

Title: Authenticated request carries a valid JWT but refers to a deleted user
Section: API Security - Subject Not Found Rejection
Preconditions: A JWT was issued for a user account that has since been deleted from the database. The token itself is still signed correctly and not expired.
Steps:
1. Send a request to a protected endpoint such as GET /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10 with 'Authorization: Bearer <valid-but-orphan-token>'. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: (Header value: 'Bearer <valid-token-of-deleted-user>'; URL = /api/orders/shop/20?page=0&limit=10)
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON body whose 'code' is 'USER_NOT_FOUND' and a message indicating no user exists for that token. No data is returned.

Title: Sign-in is attempted with a blank username or blank password
Preconditions: The /api/auth/signin endpoint is reachable. No prior authentication is required.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/signin with the JSON body shown in testData. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"username": "", "password": ""}
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized (or HTTP 400 Bad Request) with a JSON error body indicating invalid username or password. No JWT is returned.

Title: Sign-in is attempted with a valid username but wrong password
Preconditions: A user with username 'shopowner1' exists and is enabled.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/signin with the JSON body shown in testData. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"username": "shopowner1", "password": "definitely-wrong-pw"}
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON error body whose status is 'error' and message indicates invalid username or password. No JWT is issued.

Title: PIN-based login is attempted with a non-matching PIN
Preconditions: A user with phone '01711111111' exists, has a PIN already set, and the PIN currently in the database is '1234'.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/login with the JSON body shown in testData. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"username": "01711111111", "pin": "9999"}
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with a JSON error body whose status is 'error' and message indicates invalid username or PIN. No JWT is issued.

Title: Set-PIN is called with pin and confirmPin fields that do not match
Preconditions: An OTP has been issued to phone '01711111111' and is still within its validity window.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/set-pin with the JSON body shown in testData (pin and confirmPin differ). 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "01711111111", "otp": "123456", "pin": "1234", "confirmPin": "4321"}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a JSON error body whose message states that PIN and Confirm PIN do not match. The user's PIN is not changed.

Title: OTP verification is attempted with a code that does not match the stored OTP
Section: Authentication - OTP Verification with Wrong Code
Preconditions: An OTP has been issued to phone '01711111111' and is still within its validity window. The actual OTP stored for that phone is, for example, '482910'.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/auth/verify-otp with the JSON body shown in testData. 2. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"phoneNumber": "01711111111", "otp": "000000"}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a JSON error body whose message indicates the OTP is invalid or expired. No successful verification response is returned.

Title: POST /api/orders is called with a missing required shopId
Section: Order Management - Order Creation Missing Required Field
Preconditions: An authenticated shop owner exists and is signed in. The shop they own is shopId 10.
Steps:
1. Sign in as a valid shop owner and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a POST request to /api/orders with the JSON body in testData (no shopId). 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"customerName": "John Doe", "customerPhone": "01711111111", "paidAmount": 0, "items": []}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a JSON error body indicating shopId is required. No order is created.

Title: Payment endpoint is hit with a non-numeric payment amount
Preconditions: An order with id 100 exists and belongs to the authenticated shop owner. The current paidAmount is 0 and the totalAmount is 100.00.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the owner of order 100 and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a POST request to /api/orders/100/pay with the JSON body in testData. 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"paymentAmount": "abc", "paymentDate": "2026-01-15"}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a JSON error body indicating that the paymentAmount must be a valid numeric value. The order's paidAmount and dueAmount are not changed.

Title: Payment endpoint is hit with a missing paymentAmount field
Preconditions: An order with id 100 exists and belongs to the authenticated shop owner. The current paidAmount is 0 and the totalAmount is 100.00.
Steps:
1. Sign in as the owner of order 100 and obtain the bearer token. 2. Send a POST request to /api/orders/100/pay with the JSON body in testData (no paymentAmount). 3. Observe the HTTP response.

Test Data: {"paymentDate": "2026-01-15"}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a JSON error body indicating that paymentAmount is required. The order is not modified.

Title: Login with uppercase username that exists as lowercase in database (case-insensitive boundary)
Preconditions: A user account exists with username 'johndoe' (lowercase), password 'password123', and ROLE_CUSTOMER
Steps:
1. Send POST request to /api/auth/login with body {"username": "JOHNDOE", "pin": "password123"}

Test Data: {"username": "JOHNDOE", "pin": "password123"}
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK status with status 'success'. The JWT response includes the user ID and shopId, proving case-insensitive username lookup now works. Before this change, uppercase usernames would fail.

Title: Login with email address instead of username (new identifier type boundary)
Preconditions: A user account exists with email 'john.doe@example.com', password 'password123', and ROLE_CUSTOMER
Steps:
1. Send POST request to /api/auth/login with body {"username": "john.doe@example.com", "pin": "password123"}

Test Data: {"username": "john.doe@example.com", "pin": "password123"}
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK status with status 'success'. The JWT response includes the user ID. Before this change, login only accepted username and would fail with email.

Title: Login with phone number instead of username (new identifier type boundary)
Preconditions: A user account exists with phone number '+1234567890', password 'password123', and ROLE_CUSTOMER
Steps:
1. Send POST request to /api/auth/login with body {"username": "+1234567890", "pin": "password123"}

Test Data: {"username": "+1234567890", "pin": "password123"}
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK status with status 'success'. The JWT response includes the user ID. Before this change, login only accepted username and would fail with phone number.

Title: Login with blank/whitespace-only identifier (empty boundary)
Preconditions: No specific user needed - this tests input validation
Steps:
1. Send POST request to /api/auth/login with body {"username": "   ", "pin": "password123"}

Test Data: {"username": "   ", "pin": "password123"}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request or 401 Unauthorized status. The blank identifier should be trimmed and result in user not found, not cause an internal server error. Before this change, the behavior was undefined for this input.

Title: Search orders by phone as owner of shop A, expecting only shop A's orders (shopId filtering boundary)
Section: Order Search by Phone - Shop-Scoped Results
Preconditions: Two shops exist (A with ID 1, B with ID 2). Customer 'John' with phone '+1234567890' has one order in shop A and one order in shop B. Authenticated as owner of shop A.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as owner of shop A. 2. Send GET request to /api/orders/by-phone?phone=+1234567890&page=0&limit=10

Test Data: phone=+1234567890
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK with exactly 1 order in the results (only the order from shop A). Before this change, the response would include orders from BOTH shop A and shop B, proving the shopId filtering was not applied.

Title: Search orders by phone where customer has no orders in your shop (empty result boundary)
Section: Order Search by Phone - Shop-Scoped Results
Preconditions: Shop A exists with ID 1. Customer 'Jane' with phone '+9876543210' has orders only in shop B (not shop A). Authenticated as owner of shop A.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as owner of shop A. 2. Send GET request to /api/orders/by-phone?phone=+9876543210&page=0&limit=10

Test Data: phone=+9876543210
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK with empty results (totalElements: 0). Before this change, this query would return Jane's orders from shop B, proving cross-shop data leakage.

Title: Send request with expired JWT token (expiration boundary)
Preconditions: A valid JWT token that was generated with past expiration time (e.g., expired 1 minute ago)
Steps:
1. Send GET request to /api/orders/shop/1 with header "Authorization: Bearer <expired_token>"

Test Data: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzUxMiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhZG1pbiIsImV4cCI6MTcwMTIzNDg2Nn0.expired_signature
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with JSON body containing "code": "TOKEN_EXPIRED" and "message": "Your session has expired. Please login again.". Before this change, expired tokens may have been treated as generic invalid tokens without specific error messaging.

Title: Send request with malformed JWT token (malformed boundary)
Preconditions: A JWT token string that is not properly formatted (e.g., missing parts, random string)
Steps:
1. Send GET request to /api/orders/shop/1 with header "Authorization: Bearer not.a.valid.jwt.token"

Test Data: Authorization: Bearer not.a.valid.jwt.token
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with JSON body containing "code": "TOKEN_INVALID" and "message": "Invalid token. Please login again.". Before this change, malformed tokens may have caused different error responses or 500 errors.

Title: Send CORS preflight OPTIONS request to protected endpoint (OPTIONS method boundary)
Preconditions: No authentication - this tests that OPTIONS requests pass through without authentication
Steps:
1. Send OPTIONS request to /api/orders/shop/1 with headers "Origin: http://example.com", "Access-Control-Request-Method: GET", "Access-Control-Request-Headers: Authorization"

Test Data: OPTIONS /api/orders/shop/1
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK with CORS headers in response (Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, Access-Control-Allow-Headers). Before this change, OPTIONS requests may have been rejected with 401/403 because the JwtRequestFilter did not handle them.

Title: Create order for shop you don't own (ownership boundary)
Preconditions: Two shops exist (A owned by authenticated user, B owned by another user). Authenticated as owner of shop A.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as owner of shop A. 2. Send POST request to /api/orders with body containing shopId of shop B, valid customer data, and one order item.

Test Data: {"shopId": 2, "customerName": "Test Customer", "customerPhone": "+1111111111", "items": [{"itemId": 1}]}
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden with JSON body containing "code": "ACCESS_DENIED" and message indicating insufficient permissions. Before this change, the @PreAuthorize("@shopSecurity.owns") annotation did not exist, so any authenticated user could create orders for any shop.

Title: Update order belonging to a different shop (order ownership boundary)
Preconditions: Two shops exist (A and B). An order exists in shop B with orderId 100. Authenticated as owner of shop A (not shop B).
Steps:
1. Authenticate as owner of shop A. 2. Send PUT request to /api/orders/100 with body containing updated order data.

Test Data: {"customerName": "Updated Customer", "customerPhone": "+1111111111"}
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden with JSON body containing "code": "ACCESS_DENIED". Before this change, the @PreAuthorize("@shopSecurity.ownsOrder") annotation did not exist, so owners could potentially modify orders from other shops.

Title: Get last measurement for customer as owner of shop A, where customer has measurements in both shop A and shop B (shopId filtering boundary)
Preconditions: Two shops exist (A with ID 1, B with ID 2). Customer has orders with measurements in both shops. Authenticated as owner of shop A.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as owner of shop A. 2. Send GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement?phone=+1234567890&customerId=1&itemId=1 with shop context of shop A

Test Data: phone=+1234567890&customerId=1&itemId=1
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK with measurements from shop A only. Before this change, the query did not include shopId in the filter, so measurements from all shops were returned, potentially leaking business data between shops.
